text:
anya: heads-up — CI perf job on canary (runtime-v6) flagged a regression after yesterday's merge. p50 ~10% up, p99 ~2.3x, long-seq throughput down. link to perf: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/1768004310

mike: seeing the same. CI shows spike during causal-attn long-seq tests. dropping throughput on batch sizes >16.

ci-bot: perf check posted: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/1768004310/results — regression introduced between commits abc1234..def5678, p99 120ms -> 280ms on seq=2048 baseline.

jonathan: likely culprit is the kernel-selector change in PR #8124 merged last night — it prefers the fallback generic kernel for tiled layouts when swizzle mismatch is detected. I'll start a git bisect.

mike: ping when you have a commit — will try to repro locally.

jonathan: running bisect now:
```
git bisect start def5678 abc1234
git bisect run ./tools/perf/check_p99.sh --seq 2048 --model gptx
```

jonathan: bisect landed on commit b7f9c2 — "kernel-selector: prefer fallback on tiled layout". reproduces locally.

lee: fwiw I also noticed increased KV cache eviction activity in the same release acceptance tests. PR #8190 changed kv_cache.flush_on_rollout default to true which may amplify pressure during model-switch traffic. worth checking but primary signal points to kernel selector change.

sara: we need a hotfix. plan: revert the kernel-selector commit on main, then cherry-pick the revert into release/v6.1 and run perf jobs. who can open the backport PR?

mike: I can draft the revert+backport. quick revert command:
```
git revert --no-edit b7f9c2
git push origin revert/kernel-selector-regress
```
then cherry-pick the revert hash onto release/v6.1.

anya: marking rollout as blocked until hotfix is verified. @deploy-bot can you pause? :no_entry_sign:

deploy-bot: Release v6.1 rollout paused. reason=perf-regression-detected action=await-hotfix 

mike: opened PR #8205 (WIP) with the revert and a small regression test that runs the tiled-layout path under seq=2048. cc @sara @jonathan for review.

jonathan: adding an extra assertion to kernel selector unit tests to prevent falling back for this layout unless absolutely required. also adding a microbenchmark to the perf harness.

sara: for release backport I'll do: 1) create branch release/v6.1-hotfix-kernel 2) cherry-pick the revert commit 3) run perf job and smoke tests locally and in CI. exact commands:
```
git checkout -b release/v6.1-hotfix-kernel origin/release/v6.1
git cherry-pick <revert-commit-hash>
# run local perf repro
python -m perf.runner --model gptx --seq 2048 --batch-dist 'burst=0.7,steady=0.3' --kv-cache=true
```

lee: I'll prepare a hotfix build artifact and run the integration smoke tests after CI green. also can run a longer soak focusing on KV cache metrics to be safe.

mike: CI perf job queued after PR merge. can someone keep an eye on the perf dashboard? I'll tag @sara and @lee.

ci-bot: perf job queued: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/1768004322, estimated start in 8 minutes.

sara: :thumbsup: watching. also adding a note to the PR describing the revert rationale and follow-ups: (1) tighten selector thresholds (2) add KV cache telemetry for rollout scenarios.

lee: if CI perf looks good we'll cut a hotfix build and verify staging traffic for 30m before resuming rollout.

mike: plan summary: revert on main, cherry-pick revert to release/v6.1, run perf + smoke, cut hotfix artifact, verify, unpause. ETA ~2 hours assuming CI jobs behave.

anya: thanks. please update this thread with CI links and when rollout is resumed.

ci-bot: perf job completed: https://ci.internal.redwood/perf/1768004322/results — p99 back to 118ms (baseline 120ms), throughput restored for seq=2048 tests. KV metrics show no abnormal evictions in the canary run.

mike: verified the results locally as well. merging cherry-pick into release/v6.1 and publishing hotfix build now.

deploy-bot: Rollout resumed for release v6.1. reason=hotfix-applied perf-verified by CI.

sara: will follow up with a short postmortem and a defensive test PR to prevent this regression class. also scheduling a quick retro with ML infra team to align on selector heuristics.

lee: adding a perf monitor alert for sudden changes in batch-size distribution and KV eviction rate during rollouts to detect similar regressions earlier.

anya: great work everyone, nice quick coordination.
